sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:201719
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 44464 of 2023

Applicant :- Monu
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Sushil Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned AGA apprised the Court that on 06.10.2023 notice has been served upon the informant.
Despite service of notice, none present on behalf of the informant.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Sushil Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned AGA for the State.
4. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 192 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Jansath, District Muzaffar Nagar during pendency of the trial.
5. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and co-accused Ashish and according to the FIR applicant and co-accused Ashish have enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 17 years.

sentences.text:
6. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and actually victim herself had gone along with applicant and this fact is evident from her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
7.

He further submits that in the statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
victim did not state that either applicant made physical relationship with her or committed rape with her.

He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 09.08.2023.
8.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that victim in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. did not state that applicant either made physical relationship with her or committed rape with her.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
10. Considering the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C., in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Monu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 18.10.2023 AK Pandey  Monu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53785007/
